speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a pediatric patient presenting with a 3-week history of fatigue, easy bruising, fever, and severe leg pain. To begin our assessment, how old are you, and have you noticed any bone or joint swelling specifically in your legs?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing generalized fatigue and easy bruising for 3 weeks. Over the past week, she has developed a fever and severe leg pain that wakes her up at night.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Leukemia.

The patient's age (4 years old) combined with the classic triad of prolonged fatigue, easy bruising, and severe night pain strongly suggests a hematologic malignancy. Given the fever and duration, bone marrow infiltration is the primary concern. I will proceed with immediate laboratory testing to confirm the diagnosis.

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential and peripheral smear.
REQUEST TEST: Coagulation profile (PT/PTT/Platelets).
REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis.
REQUEST IMAGES: No immediate imaging required; blood work is diagnostic priority.
